class: Controls drawn inside a list's own options were read as questions of their own
symptom: Ciena on Workday, 30 September: after the degrees were entered, Workday's Field of Study list stayed open; the agent 'answered' Accounting, Advertising, African Languages ... one subject at a time for three minutes, which the owner saw as the run looping again.
site: Workday (multi-select prompts draw a radio inside each option); any site that draws a tick or radio inside list options
root_cause: parse_snapshot made a question of every radio/checkbox with a reference, named by the text after it; it did not look at what the control sat inside, so each option of an open listbox became a question.
why_tests_missed: Snapshots in the tests had lists closed, or options without their own radio pictures.
fix: parse_snapshot keeps the indents of the list options (and open lists) a line sits inside; a radio or tick inside one is that choice's picture and is skipped. Radios inside ordinary list items (Yes/No drawn as a list) are still questions.
prevention: A control's meaning depends on what it sits inside: read the ancestor roles (option, menu, listbox) before making a question of it.
